title: Test your ETL vs ELT basics

questions.q: In the kitchen picture from the post, ETL preps the food in a back room and ELT sends raw ingredients straight to the counter. So what really separates ETL from ELT?
options: How many people use the data afterwards
Whether the data comes from a database or from files
Where the cleaning and reshaping step happens
Whether the data is ever stored at all
questions.explain: The only real difference is where the transform step runs. ETL cleans data in a separate engine before loading. ELT loads it raw and cleans it inside the target.

questions.q: Your company has a modern warehouse or lakehouse that can scale up easily. Which pattern does the post say fits best?
options: ELT, because the target can do the cleaning itself
ETL, because a big target needs a second engine
Neither, because big targets can't clean data
Whichever tool is cheapest to buy
questions.explain: When the target has room to scale, ELT lets it do the transform work, so you skip a whole extra system. A weak or small target is where ETL starts to make sense.

questions.q: A rule says personal data must be checked or masked before it lands anywhere. Which fits that rule most naturally?
options: ELT, because raw data is easier to protect
Neither, because rules only apply to reports
ELT, because masking never works on raw data
ETL, because the data is cleaned before loading
questions.explain: With ETL, personal data can be masked before it reaches the target, so the real values never land. ELT can still be made safe, but it leans on access controls inside the target.

questions.q: Someone says, "ELT only works if you own a data warehouse." What does the post say about that?
options: True, ELT is built for warehouses only
A myth, since ELT can start from files in cheap storage
True, unless the data is very small
A myth, because ELT skips the transform step
questions.explain: Nope, that's a myth. ELT can start with files in scalable storage and a lakehouse works too. The target does need enough compute to transform data well. And ELT still transforms, just later.

questions.q: Your company has some sources with strict privacy rules and others where analysts want raw data to explore. What does the post suggest?
options: Pick ELT for everything, to keep things simple
Pick ETL for everything, to be safe
Choose per source, and mix both if that fits
Wait until one pattern clearly wins
questions.explain: Don't pick one pattern for the whole company. Many teams use ETL for the few sources with strict rules and ELT for the rest. Just write down which source uses which path.
